risk_if_not_implemented: Without Security, Compliance & Resilience Protection Portfolio Management, security, compliance and resilience requirements may be omitted from projects and initiatives until late, costly stages. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, no risk is rated Likely; risks rated Possible include Business / Service Interruption (R-BC-1), Reduced Operational Productivity (R-BC-3), Regulatory / Legal / Contractual Financial Liability (R-EX-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Risk Management Program
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of strategic, operational and tactical risk management controls that are aligned with:
(1) The organization's Enterprise Risk Management (ERM); and
(2) Industry-recognized cybersecurity risk management practices.
compensating_control_1.justification: Risk Management Program (RSK-02) provides policy-level governance that compensates for the absence of Security, Compliance & Resilience Protection Portfolio Management (PRM-04) by establishing documented expectations, accountability structures, and organizational guardrails. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Security, Compliance & Resilience Program (SCRP)
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the design, implementation, and monitoring of security, compliance and resilience governance controls.
compensating_control_2.justification: Security, Compliance & Resilience Program (SCRP) (GOV-02) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Security, Compliance & Resilience Protection Portfolio Management (PRM-04) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
